summary: Geshe Ngawang Samten studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1980) and Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1980–1990). Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he served as Chief Editor at CIHTS (~1987–2021) alongside several visiting professorships.
Geshe Palden Dragpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as Librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, where he is attested from 1987 to 1992 and in 2004.

Geshe Palden Drakpa specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as Librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, attested in 1988.

Geshe Rabten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and founded Rabten Choeling in 1977.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, later serving as resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from 1978.

Geshe Tashi Tsering works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1970–1990) and Gyuto Monastery, later holding teaching positions at Kopan Monastery (~1992–1994) and Jamyang Buddhist Centre from 1994.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Tenzin Dhargye studied at Sera Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He taught at the University of Virginia (1999–2000) and became director of Tibetzentrum Österreich in 2008.
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his Geshe studies at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Agvan Dorjiev and at Drepung Monastery. He taught at Columbia University (~1962–1972) and founded the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, serving there from ~1958 to 1983.
Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1991, 2004, and from 2014 to 2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) under teachers including Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from ~1967 to 1971.
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served at Otani University as lecturer, professor, and president (1924–1925), and founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921.

Gherardo Gnoli studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1954–1958) in Iranian/Central Asian and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Naples (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008), and served as president of IsMEO (1979–1995) and IsIAO (1995–2011).

Ghulam Yazdani studied at Aligarh Muslim University (~1903–1905) in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Government College Lahore, and served as Director of Archæology for the Government of Hyderabad (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Sapienza University of Rome under Raniero Gnoli, and began teaching at "L'Orientale" around 1998.
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda studied at Kyoto University (~1911–1914) in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served on the faculty at Kyoto University (1929; 1935–1948) and held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology, earning his doctorate at Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (assistant in 1940, lecturer in 1947, professor 1968–1972) and later at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).
